protocol: Naya/ILS 0.3 thermogravimetry, single SDT calibration group, pre-outcome transfer

source.primary: Naya et al., 2014, DOI10.1007/s10973-014-4039-1, Experimental and Table 1
source.axes: ILS authors’ ils.fqcs example uses 1000 equally spaced 40…850 °C inclusive and mass %. Furnace ramp was 20…900 °C,20°C/min under air50mL/min. Packaged comparison grid only. Independently bind published code literals and preserve actual array dimensions/axis coordinates; refuse if an explicitly labeled numeric physical-temperature axis contradicts the example. Generic ordinal dimnames not temperature evidence.
source.apparatus: Physical specimens:15 per group. 2–5, four reference operators under common calibration on one SDT2960; 6, another operator with two-year-old calibration; 7, another operator applying erroneous zinc-point reference displaced2°C, sign and full calibration map unspecified. Group1 different rheometric STA1500 with old calibration. These are a simulated interlaboratory design using actual measurements; six SDT labels share one instrument, each altered setting confounded with operator. No randomization/order inference from release ordinal.
source.scope: 105 TG real curves only. DSC and IDT payloads stay unmapped. One manufacturer/purity (99%+ calcium oxalate monohydrate) and ramp. The authors’ reports of group7 as outlier and its qualitative final-step difference are exposed; numerical outcomes unseen. Comparator task = prospective computational forecast on an archival cohort, not independent replication of author analysis.

budget.reference: All 60 complete source curves, groups2–5, rows1–15. Three disjoint 5-specimen training blocks per group for empirical model. No one-to-one cross-group specimen pairing.
budget.calibration: Groups1,6,7: release rows1–5 early T≤280°C only. Use arithmetic group mean curve. No held specimen value at any T used to choose forecasts.
budget.evaluation: Each complete later trajectory of remaining distinct release specimens6–15 of groups1,6,7. Primary group7 one operator/setting with10 new specimens. Other groups1,6 reported as explicit out-of-family checks with no known imposed zinc error. No selection based on score. Deserialization can materialize all TG bytes but only selected slices are passed into forecast construction. Later measured rows of target groups remain numerically unexamined until prediction lock. DSC.RData,IDT.RData and group7 outcome tests stay separated.

reference_chemistry: Heating monohydrate separates dehydration, oxalate→carbonate and decarbonation. At one imposed ramp, a temperature offset and a differing thermal lag can agree (δT=20δt). Operator, sample behavior, calibration and heat transfer remain possible. A single zinc constraint cannot determine a full calibration function. Candidate tests an affine approximation for archived mass transfer, not a traceable calibration measurement.

estimator.vertical: Subtract target-reference baseline differences only via one offset equal to mean difference at45–70°C. Apply same offset to every temperature-map role; retain uncorrected template separately.
estimator.landmarks: For each early mean, early high plateau mean45–70, low plateau mean235–270; crossing fractions .15,.325,.50,.675,.85 of high−low on 75–235°C. First downward linear interpolated threshold crossing, no smoothing. Refuse missing/zero-amplitude/nonfinite crossing. Midpoint and 15–85% width reported.
estimator.candidate: For each s∈{−1,+1}, fit T_observed−T_zinc−s·2 = a(T_reference−T_zinc) least-squares across five early landmarks; choose smaller sum of squared early temperature residuals, deterministic minus on exact tie. T_zinc=419.527°C is a convention; reported error magnitude is not proof either physical map is affine or passes exactly through this anchor. No physical bound on slope beyond positive requirement, refuse if nonpositive. Use inverse map for interpolation, clipping query to source grid endpoints. Keep both sign branches and early fit evidence.
estimator.controls: Raw reference mean, vertically corrected reference, unconstrained best early translation (mean paired shift), unconstrained early affine OLS, pure constant ±2°C shift choosing lower early SSE; nominal gain anchored at40°C plus ±2 by zinc choosing lower early SSE; actual two signed candidate curves; reference-trained low-dimensional mass ridge; late target-independent inverse maps. No fit to late target observations.
estimator.empirical: Build12 disjoint 5-specimen reference group blocks. For each block compare its mean curve to mean over the other3 whole source groups. Features: mean of five early landmark shifts, target minus reference 15–85% transition width, target minus reference 45–70 and235–270 plateau mass means. Regress raw target late-mass minus reference late-mass as a function of early features, centering and scaling by population SD on all12 blocks (set SD=1 if zero), unpenalized intercept, fixed ridge penalty1 on standardized feature weights, all temperatures fit simultaneously. No target labels; overlapping reference templates do not create independent treatment units.

endpoints.whole: Primary equal-specimen mean RMSE in % of initial mass across all grid temperatures320 through850°C. Also report unweighted MAE, independent second-stage320≤T<560 and third-stage560≤T≤850 RMSE, all 30 per-specimen results and full signed worst physical sample with every role at that exact cell. Inspect ±4 grid-cell neighborhood and same-temperature all10 specimen residuals without retuning.
endpoints.gate: Group7 sign-selected zinc-affine candidate strictly beats vertically matched unshifted, early translation, unconstrained affine, selected constant2, selected gain and ridge mean RMSE. It must beat early translation separately in both stage windows and beat empirical ridge on ≥6/10 primary specimens. The two individually fixed-sign zinc maps are diagnostic arms, one equals the selected candidate. No CI across calibration conditions or inferred calibration attribution. Secondary controls cannot rescue primary failure.
endpoints.raw: Output every temperature/role prediction before accessing later observations and lock source byte identities, both signed fits, reference and calibration geometry, and scope. All observations scored from original frozen file, identical indices and mass % units. No target-dependent coordinate adjustment, filtering, tail removal or replacement.
